newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CARACAS SHARES END FIRM AS STRIKE GOES PEACEFULLY.
newsitem.headline: CARACAS SHARES END FIRM AS STRIKE GOES PEACEFULLY.

text.p: Venezuelan stocks closed higher on Wednesday despite a 12-hour national work stoppage, as investors took heart that the strike went ahead peacefully, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the Caracas Stock Exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 1.84 percent to 9,454.25, as 35 stocks rose, three fell and five closed flat.
"Investors looked to take positions in view of the fact that the stoppage is going ahead peacefully," said Capitales Noroco broker Jose Gregorio Tineo.

Labor unions staged Wednesday's strike to press private-sector companies to raise wages. The walkout closed down government offices and halted public transport, though other public services and the stock and currency markets operated normally.
Brokers said the market would put the strike behind it Thursday and resume its recent bullish trend.
Trading volume was lighter than usual, brokers said, with just 1,204 trades of shares worth 4.593 billion bolivars ($9.3 million).

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 13.25 bolivars to 823.25 bolivars, telephone company CANTV rose 25.00 bolivars to 3,070.00 bolivars and steel company Sivensa slipped 4.25 bolivars to 272.00 bolivars.

Brokers said there was particular interest in holding company H.L. Boulton, which rose 5.00 bolivars to 52.00 bolivars and dominated the day's trade, surpassing even Electricidad. One broker said strong full-year results led many investors to expect H.L. Boulton to announce a big dividend.
